title: 2 Timothy Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Timothy chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Timothy Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Timothy Chapter 4.

questions.question: Who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the Lord Jesus Christ shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom. (2 Timothy 4:1)

questions.question: What are believers instructed to do in 2 Timothy 4:2?
questions.explanation: The instruction given is to 'Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season...' (2 Timothy 4:2)

questions.question: True or False: Paul indicates that there will be a time when people will endure sound doctrine.
questions.explanation: Paul states that 'the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine...' (2 Timothy 4:3), indicating they will not endure it.

questions.question: According to 2 Timothy 4:4, what will people turn away from?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables. (2 Timothy 4:4)

questions.question: What does Paul instruct Timothy to do in all things?
questions.explanation: Paul instructs Timothy to 'But watch thou in all things...' (2 Timothy 4:5).

questions.question: True or False: Paul is ready to depart and be offered.
questions.explanation: Paul states, 'For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.' (2 Timothy 4:6)

questions.question: What does Paul claim to have kept?
questions.explanation: Paul states, 'I have kept the faith:' indicating he has maintained his faith. (2 Timothy 4:7)

questions.question: What is laid up for Paul according to 2 Timothy 4:8?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions that 'Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness...' (2 Timothy 4:8).

questions.question: True or False: Paul mentions that only Luke is with him.
questions.explanation: Paul states, 'Only Luke is with me.' indicating Luke is the only companion at that time. (2 Timothy 4:11)

questions.question: What did Paul ask Timothy to bring when he comes?
questions.explanation: Paul requests, 'bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.' (2 Timothy 4:13).

questions.question: True or False: Demas remained with Paul because he loved the present world.
questions.explanation: Demas forsook Paul 'having loved this present world...' showing he departed instead of remaining. (2 Timothy 4:10)

questions.question: What did Paul say about Alexander the coppersmith?
questions.explanation: Paul states, 'Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil...' indicating his negative actions. (2 Timothy 4:14)

questions.question: In 2 Timothy 4, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
questions.explanation: The first instruction given in the chapter is to 'Preach the word...' (2 Timothy 4:2).

medium.title: 2 Timothy Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Timothy Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Paul charge Timothy to do in 2 Timothy 4:2?
questions.explanation: Paul instructs Timothy to 'Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season' which emphasizes the importance of consistently sharing the Gospel. (2 Timothy 4:2)

questions.question: According to 2 Timothy 4:3, what will people not endure?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine', indicating a shift away from biblical teachings. (2 Timothy 4:3)

questions.question: What does Paul say about his departure in 2 Timothy 4:6?
options: He is going on a journey
He is ready to be offered
He is moving to a new city
questions.correctAnswer: He is ready to be offered
questions.explanation: In this verse, Paul expresses that 'I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand', indicating his impending martyrdom. (2 Timothy 4:6)

questions.question: What does Paul mention as being laid up for him in 2 Timothy 4:8?
questions.explanation: Paul speaks of a 'crown of righteousness' that is laid up for him, which he will receive from the Lord. (2 Timothy 4:8)

questions.question: What does 2 Timothy 4:10 reveal about Demas?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that 'Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world', showing his departure from Paul. (2 Timothy 4:10)

questions.question: Who does Paul say is with him in 2 Timothy 4:11?
questions.explanation: Paul states that 'Only Luke is with me', emphasizing the loyalty of Luke during his imprisonment. (2 Timothy 4:11)

questions.question: In 2 Timothy 4:12, where has Paul sent Tychicus?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions that 'And Tychicus have I sent to Ephesus', indicating his trust in Tychicus to minister there. (2 Timothy 4:12)

questions.question: What does Paul request Timothy to bring in 2 Timothy 4:13?
questions.explanation: Paul specifically asks for 'the cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments'. (2 Timothy 4:13)

questions.question: True or False: Alexander the coppersmith did Paul good according to 2 Timothy 4:14.
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil', indicating he harmed Paul rather than helped him. (2 Timothy 4:14)

questions.question: True or False: No one stood with Paul at his first answer according to 2 Timothy 4:16.
questions.explanation: Paul states in this verse that 'no man stood with me, but all men forsook me', highlighting his isolation at that moment. (2 Timothy 4:16)

questions.question: What does Paul express about God's support in 2 Timothy 4:17?
questions.explanation: Paul affirms that 'Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me', indicating God's presence and support during his trials. (2 Timothy 4:17)

questions.question: What does Paul say about the Lord's deliverance in 2 Timothy 4:18?
options: He will deliver him from every evil work
He will bless him with riches
He will send him to safety
He will heal him from sickness
questions.correctAnswer: He will deliver him from every evil work
questions.explanation: Paul expresses confidence that 'the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work', emphasizing God's protection. (2 Timothy 4:18)

questions.question: True or False: Paul instructs Timothy to come before winter in 2 Timothy 4:21.
questions.explanation: Paul indeed urges Timothy to 'Do thy diligence to come before winter', indicating the urgency of his request. (2 Timothy 4:21)

hard.title: 2 Timothy Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Timothy Chapter 4.

questions.question: Who does Paul charge Timothy to preach before?
questions.explanation: Paul charges Timothy before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, as stated in 2 Timothy 4:1.

questions.question: What should Timothy do in addition to preaching the word?
questions.explanation: Timothy is instructed to reprove, rebuke, and exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine in 2 Timothy 4:2.

questions.question: What will happen when people do not endure sound doctrine?
questions.explanation: According to 2 Timothy 4:3, people will heap to themselves teachers after their own lusts, having itching ears.

questions.question: What does Paul say he has kept?
questions.explanation: Paul states in 2 Timothy 4:7 that he has kept the faith throughout his ministry.

questions.question: What does Paul say is laid up for him?
questions.explanation: In 2 Timothy 4:8, Paul mentions that there is a crown of righteousness laid up for him, which the Lord will give him.

questions.question: Did Paul have any companions with him at his first answer?
questions.explanation: Paul states in 2 Timothy 4:16 that no man stood with him, indicating he was alone at his first answer.

questions.question: Which character did Paul mention as having done him much evil?
questions.explanation: In 2 Timothy 4:14, Paul refers to Alexander the coppersmith as one who did him much evil.

questions.question: True or False: Paul expresses a desire for Timothy to come before winter.
questions.explanation: In 2 Timothy 4:21, Paul urges Timothy to do his diligence to come before winter, indicating the urgency of his request.

questions.question: What does Paul say about the Lord's role in his preaching?
questions.explanation: Paul states in 2 Timothy 4:17 that the Lord stood with him and strengthened him for the preaching to be fully known.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'crown of righteousness' in this chapter?
options: It is a metaphor for struggle
questions.explanation: The 'crown of righteousness' mentioned in 2 Timothy 4:8 symbolizes the eternal reward for those who love His appearing.

questions.question: True or False: Paul mentions that Trophimus was sick and left at Miletum.
questions.explanation: In 2 Timothy 4:20, Paul indeed states that he left Trophimus at Miletum sick.

questions.question: What does Paul request Timothy to bring with him when he comes?
questions.explanation: In 2 Timothy 4:13, Paul specifically asks Timothy to bring the cloak and the books when he comes.

questions.question: Which Old Testament theme echoes in Paul's statement about being delivered from the mouth of the lion?
questions.explanation: The phrase connects to the theme of deliverance found in Psalm 22:21, where the psalmist speaks of being saved from the lion's mouth, paralleling Paul's experience in 2 Timothy 4:17.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Paul's exhortation to Timothy in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Paul employs parallelism in his structure of exhortation, particularly in the encouragement to preach and endure in 2 Timothy 4:2-5.

theological.title: 2 Timothy Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Timothy Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What charge does Paul give Timothy in 2 Timothy 4:1?
options: To judge the quick and the dead
questions.explanation: Paul charges Timothy to 'Preach the word' (2 Timothy 4:2) and emphasizes this as a key responsibility before God and Christ.

questions.question: According to 2 Timothy 4:3, what will people not endure?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine' (2 Timothy 4:3), indicating a rejection of biblical truth.

questions.question: What should Timothy do in response to the challenges mentioned in 2 Timothy 4:5?
options: Make full proof of his ministry
questions.correctAnswer: Make full proof of his ministry
questions.explanation: Paul instructs Timothy to 'do the work of an evangelist, make full proof of thy ministry' (2 Timothy 4:5), urging diligence in his calling.

questions.question: In 2 Timothy 4:6, what does Paul indicate about his current situation?
options: He is ready to be offered
questions.correctAnswer: He is ready to be offered
questions.explanation: Paul states, 'I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand' (2 Timothy 4:6), revealing his awareness of his imminent death.

questions.question: What does Paul claim to have accomplished in 2 Timothy 4:7?
questions.explanation: Paul asserts, 'I have finished my course' (2 Timothy 4:7), indicating his fulfillment of his ministry and life mission.

questions.question: What does the 'crown of righteousness' refer to in 2 Timothy 4:8?
questions.explanation: In this verse, Paul mentions a 'crown of righteousness' which signifies a reward for those who have loved Christ's appearing, reflecting their faithfulness (2 Timothy 4:8).

questions.question: Who does Paul mention as having forsaken him in 2 Timothy 4:10?
questions.explanation: Paul notes that 'Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world' (2 Timothy 4:10), highlighting a tragic abandonment.

questions.question: What does Paul ask Timothy to bring him in 2 Timothy 4:13?
questions.explanation: Paul requests, 'The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books' (2 Timothy 4:13), showing his need for comfort and study materials.

questions.question: According to 2 Timothy 4:14, what did Alexander the coppersmith do to Paul?
questions.explanation: Paul warns that 'Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil' (2 Timothy 4:14), indicating a significant betrayal and harm by this individual.

questions.question: What does Paul express about those who forsook him in 2 Timothy 4:16?
questions.explanation: Paul states, 'I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge' (2 Timothy 4:16), showing his desire for mercy towards those who abandoned him.

questions.question: What significant event does Paul refer to in 2 Timothy 4:17?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions, 'I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion' (2 Timothy 4:17), which may symbolize his rescue from peril or persecution.

questions.question: What does 2 Timothy 4:18 indicate about the Lord's protection?
options: He will deliver from evil works
He will give a long life
He will ensure victory in battles
questions.correctAnswer: He will deliver from evil works
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'And the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work' (2 Timothy 4:18), affirming God's promise of protection and deliverance.

questions.question: To whom does Paul send greetings in 2 Timothy 4:19?
questions.explanation: Paul specifically greets 'Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus' (2 Timothy 4:19), showing his connection and affection for them.

questions.question: What does Paul say about Erastus in 2 Timothy 4:20?
questions.explanation: Paul notes, 'Erastus abode at Corinth' (2 Timothy 4:20), providing information about the whereabouts of his fellow worker.

questions.question: What urgent request does Paul make in 2 Timothy 4:21?
questions.explanation: Paul urges Timothy to 'Do thy diligence to come before winter' (2 Timothy 4:21), indicating the importance of his timely arrival.
